lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Launch and diagnostic: dilation, center, and scale factor

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Read the example first. You are not expected to know this yet.

items.prompt: Dilate (3, −2) about the origin by factor 4.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Try each one. If you get stuck, write what you do know and move on.

items.prompt: A figure is dilated so that a side of length 6 becomes a side of length 12. What is the scale factor, and what happens to the figure's area?
choices: scale factor 2; the area is multiplied by 2
scale factor 6; the area is multiplied by 4
scale factor 2; the area is multiplied by 4
scale factor 1/2; the area is multiplied by 4

items.prompt: Triangle ABC has ∠A = 53° and ∠B = 89°. Triangle DEF has ∠D = 53° and ∠E = 89°. Are the triangles similar, and on what grounds?
choices: No; angle information alone never establishes similarity.
Yes, by AA similarity: two pairs of congruent angles force the third pair to be congruent as well.
Yes, by SSS similarity.
Yes, but only if a pair of corresponding sides is also known to be congruent.

items.prompt: Under a dilation, a segment not through the centre, under a dilation with scale factor k …
choices: is mapped to a parallel segment k times as long
is mapped to a segment of the same length
is mapped to a segment k² times as long
is mapped to a perpendicular segment k times as long

items.prompt: Dilate the point (4, 3) about the origin with scale factor 2. Give the image.
A figure is dilated so that a side of length 16 becomes a side of length 32. What is the scale factor, and what happens to the figure's area?
choices: scale factor 2; the area is multiplied by 2
scale factor 2; the area is multiplied by 4
scale factor 16; the area is multiplied by 4
scale factor 1/2; the area is multiplied by 4

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Show what you can do so far. This sets the starting point, not a grade.

items.prompt: Triangle ABC has ∠A = 33° and ∠B = 109°. Triangle DEF has ∠D = 33° and ∠E = 109°. Are the triangles similar, and on what grounds?
choices: Yes, but only if a pair of corresponding sides is also known to be congruent.
Yes, by SSS similarity.
No; angle information alone never establishes similarity.
Yes, by AA similarity: two pairs of congruent angles force the third pair to be congruent as well.

items.prompt: Under a dilation, a line that does not pass through the centre of dilation …
choices: is mapped onto itself
is mapped to a line with slope multiplied by the scale factor
is mapped to a perpendicular line
is mapped to a parallel line
